analysis.title: Oklo Inc. (OKLO.N): Money in the Bank, Milestones on the Board, Execution Up Next
key_insights: Oklo beat 3Q26 EPS (reported -$0.22 vs Citi -$0.25 and Street -$0.26), reaffirmed guidance, and gave one of its most comprehensive updates since going public. Citi says clear NTM targets plus a beat and reaffirmed guidance should improve investor confidence.

2027 goals include fabrication of the first assemblies at the Aurora Fuel Fabrication Facility (A3F), a recycling pilot facility, the start of Groves-2 construction, and the first contracted isotope delivery.

Citi describes the balance sheet as largely de-risked. This allowed Oklo to make the ARMEC and CEI acquisitions to strengthen internal execution and to contract component delivery from U.S. Forged Rings for 27 future powerhouses.

Aurora-ID startup is now expected in late-2028/early-2029 versus 2028 previously, reflecting additional commissioning and testing time. The DSA for the ID reactor will be closer to construction completion. Pre-application is ongoing for Aurora Ohio, Eielson Air Base and the recycling facility.

Groves 1 was completed in 229 days at capex of about $65mm plus about $10mm of fuel costs. Oklo has secured fuel for Groves 2 and plans to start construction in 2027. Citi expects G2 capex to be meaningfully higher than G1 given larger scope, fuel load, more components (isotope separation) and commercial output.
Oklo signed an agreement with U.S. Forged Rings reserving forging capacity for 27 Aurora modules through 2035.

A3F fuel fabrication remains on track, with the first full fuel assembly targeted for 2027. The facility could also offer third-party metallic fuel fabrication to other reactor developers. Oklo has started NRC pre-application activities for fuel recycling.

Management highlighted potential access to the DOE's >$50B Nuclear Waste Fund as a funding source for eligible fuel recycling and waste management infrastructure, subject to future Congressional action. Clarity on plutonium allocation is expected in the next few months.
A more comprehensive update will likely come at the 1H27 analyst day or with 4Q26 results.

Citi keeps Neutral / High Risk with a $33 target price (41.8% expected return, unchanged). It says it awaits progress on the regulatory process to be more constructive. It lowered its opex outlook modestly given the recent run-rate.

market_movers.rationale: Neutral / High Risk rating and $33 target unchanged after the 3Q26 beat. Citi wants more regulatory progress before turning more constructive. Price was $23.28 on 11/6, implying 41.8% expected return.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 revenue reported $1.9mm vs Citi estimate $2.0mm and Visible Alpha consensus $1.3mm.
3Q26 total operating expenses reported $83.2mm vs Citi estimate $89.8mm and consensus $66.9mm. Interest income $27.9mm vs Citi $27.5mm and consensus $23.0mm.
3Q26 net loss reported -$41.7mm vs Citi -$47.6mm and consensus -$43.0mm. GAAP diluted EPS reported -$0.22 vs Citi estimate -$0.25 and consensus -$0.26 (3Q25: -$0.20, 2Q26: -$0.28).
FY26 guidance reiterated: operating cash burn $120-150mm and capex $400-500mm. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were $3.1B at the end of 3Q26.
Citi FY26E EPS -$1.04 (previously -$1.06) vs First Call consensus -$0.97. FY27E -$1.33 (previously -$1.61) vs consensus -$1.16. FY28E -$1.57 (previously -$1.80) vs consensus -$1.23.
risk_factors: Fuel: no commercial domestic supply of HALEU fuel currently.
Execution: nuclear facilities are prone to delays and cost overruns. Aurora-ID startup already slipped to late-2028/early-2029.
Technology: though the technology is de-risked through operation at EBR, widescale deployment carries risk.
Financing: Oklo may need substantial outside capital long term if it deploys plants at the targeted pace.
High Risk rating reflects limited operating history as a public company and expected lack of revenue until first powerhouse deployment.
Groves 2 capex is likely to be meaningfully higher than Groves 1.
Upside risks to the target: faster licensing approval, binding customer contracts, faster powerhouse deployment.
